title: Active-arrow envelope: evaluation and cocartesian-edge criterion
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors and simplicial pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and symmetric infinity-operads, active arrows and inert edges as defined in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]. Let $p:\mathcal C^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ be an inert-preserving map of symmetric infinity-operads whose underlying simplicial map is an inner fibration and has the following equivalence-lifting property: for every object $c$ and every equivalence $h:p(c)\to o$ there is an equivalence $\widetilde h:c\to c\prime$ with $p(\widetilde h)=h$. Define $\operatorname{Act}(\mathcal O^\otimes)$ to be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal O^\otimes)$ on active edges. Form the degreewise pullback
$$H=\mathcal C^\otimes\times_{p,\mathcal O^\otimes,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Act}(\mathcal O^\otimes),\qquad r=\operatorname{ev}_1:H\to\mathcal O^\otimes.$$
An object of $H$ is a pair $(c,a:p(c)\to o)$ with $a$ active; a morphism consists of an edge in $\mathcal C^\otimes$ and its coherent square between the active arrows, retaining all higher simplices. Then $H$, with the composite $H\xrightarrow{r}\mathcal O^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, is a symmetric infinity-operad, $r$ is an inert-preserving cocartesian fibration, and an edge of $H$ is $r$-cocartesian if and only if its image under $H\to\mathcal C^\otimes$ is inert in $\mathcal C^\otimes$.

source.place: Definition 2.1.2.10 (fibration hypothesis); Construction 2.2.4.1, Proposition 2.2.4.4, Lemma 2.2.4.15(3)-(4), printed pp. 211-212 and 216-218 (PDF pages 210-211 and 215-217). September 18, 2017 edition read online. WANTED archive in literature/. No Stacks tag treats symmetric infinity-operads or this envelope.

proof.text:
Write $s_C:\mathcal C^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and $s_O:\mathcal O^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. The given inner-fibration and equivalence-lifting hypotheses on $p$ are exactly those required by [lem-coef-infinity-lax-comma-target-fibration]. Apply it to form the unrestricted arrow category $T$ and its inner fibration $q:T\to\mathcal O^\otimes$. The specified $H$ is its full subcategory on pairs with active arrow: a simplex lies in this subcategory precisely when all its vertices do. An inner horn already contains every vertex of its simplex, so a filler in $T$ of a lifting problem for $H\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ belongs to $H$. Thus $r$ is an inner fibration, $H$ is a quasicategory, and $s_Or$ is an inner fibration by lifting first in $\mathcal O^\otimes$ and then in $H$. The comma mapping formula restricts unchanged to $H$ because its mapping simplices have only the two endpoint vertices. For $x=(c,a:p(c)\to o)$ and $z=(d,b:p(d)\to t)$ it is
$$\operatorname{Map}_H(x,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^\otimes}(c,d)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}(p(c),t)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}(o,t).$$

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1 and Lemma 2.2.4.15(1)-(2): unrestricted arrow category, then full active subcategory; explicit horn and mapping-space verification.

proof.text: Every inert edge $f:c\to c'$ of $\mathcal C^\otimes$ is $p$-cocartesian. Indeed it is $s_C$-cocartesian, and $p(f)$ is $s_O$-cocartesian by inert preservation. Apply the mapping criterion to both and cancel the lower homotopy-pullback square using [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting]; the remaining square is exactly the $p$-cocartesian square. Moreover every specified inert $j:p(c)\to v$ has an inert lift with source $c$ and image exactly $j$. Choose an inert $f_0:c\to d$ over the underlying pointed map. The $s_O$-cocartesian universal properties of $p(f_0)$ and $j$ give a comparison equivalence $e:p(d)\to v$ and a triangle $e p(f_0)\simeq j$: comparison maps in both directions are inverse since precomposition with either cocartesian edge is an equivalence on the appropriate mapping-space fibers. Lift $e$ to an equivalence $\widetilde e:d\to d'$ using the hypothesis on $p$. Lift that base triangle through the inner horn with edges $f_0,\widetilde e$ using that $p$ is an inner fibration. Its third edge $f:c\to d'$ maps exactly to $j$. Inert edges are closed under composition with equivalences, so $f$ is inert. This is where the equivalence-lifting hypothesis is used.

source.place: Definition 2.1.2.10 and Proposition 2.1.2.22; elementary construction of the specified inert lift, and the mapping-space cancellation of HTT Proposition 2.4.1.3.

proof.text:
Consider an edge $e:x=(c,a)\to y=(c',a')$ of $H$ with source component $f:c\to c'$ inert and target component $g:o\to o'$, so $g a\simeq a'p(f)$. Fix $z=(d,b:p(d)\to t)$ and a map $h:o'\to t$. In the mapping formula of step 1, lifting an arrow $x\to z$ over $hg$ through $e$ asks for $u':c'\to d$ and a homotopy $b p(u')\simeq h a'$, with the specified original $u:c\to d$ and $b p(u)\simeq h g a$. Apply inert-active orthogonality to the square in $\mathcal O^\otimes$ with left side $p(f)$, right side $b$, top $p(u)$ and bottom $h a'$. Its entire space of diagonal fillers is contractible. For each such diagonal, the $p$-cocartesian square for $f$ from step 2 gives a contractible space of lifts $u'$ with the required homotopy $u'f\simeq u$. Equivalently, pasting these two homotopy-pullback squares with the formula of step 1 gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_H(y,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_H(x,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}(o,t)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}(o',t).$$
These are equivalences of spaces with all path coordinates, not just existence or uniqueness on components. The mapping criterion for the inner fibration $r$ now proves that $e$ is $r$-cocartesian.

source.place: Lemmas 2.2.4.14-2.2.4.15: explicit orthogonality/mapping-square proof of the inert-source implication, replacing the reflective-localization shorthand.

proof.text: Let $x=(c,a:p(c)\to o)$ and let $g:o\to o'$ be any edge. Form a composite $ga$ and factor it as $p(c)\xrightarrow{j}v\xrightarrow{a'}o'$ with $j$ inert and $a'$ active. Lift $j$ inertly as in step 2. The factorization triangle and the composition triangle give a coherent square, hence an edge $x\to(c',a')$ of $H$ over $g$, whose source component is inert. Step 3 proves it is $r$-cocartesian. There is therefore a cocartesian lift of every $g$, so $r$ is a cocartesian fibration. To prove the converse edge criterion, compare any $r$-cocartesian $e:x\to y$ with the constructed lift $e_0:x\to y_0$ over the same $g$. Their mapping-square universal properties give arrows $v:y_0\to y$ and $w:y\to y_0$ over the identity with $ve_0\simeq e$ and $we\simeq e_0$. Applying the same mapping equivalences to these identities gives $wv\simeq1$ and $vw\simeq1$. Thus $v$ is an equivalence, its image in $\mathcal C^\otimes$ is an equivalence, and the source component of $e$ is the composite of an inert edge with that equivalence. It is inert by [lem-coef-operadic-inert-active-factorization].

source.place: Lemma 2.2.4.15(3)-(4): construct the lift by inert-active factorization, and compare arbitrary universal lifts by their mapping-space properties.

proof.text: Every inert pointed map $\delta:s_O(o)\to\langle n\rangle$ lifts inertly from $o$ in $\mathcal O^\otimes$. Lift that edge $r$-cocartesianly from any $x$ above $o$. The two mapping squares, for $r$ and $s_O$, paste to the mapping square for $s_Or$. Hence this edge is $(s_Or)$-cocartesian. This supplies inert lifts in $H$. It also shows that $r$ preserves all inert edges: given any inert edge of $H$, compare it with this constructed lift over the same pointed map using the two universal mapping properties, as in step 4. The comparison in $H$ is an equivalence; its image in $\mathcal O^\otimes$ is an equivalence, so the image of the original edge is inert. For an inert pointed edge $\rho:\langle n\rangle\to\langle k\rangle$, the restriction $E_\rho=H\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*),\rho}\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ is a cocartesian fibration, and the constructed lifts above are $E_\rho$-cocartesian: inner-horn fillers and the horn conditions for the constructed cocartesian edges restrict by projecting a lifting problem to that edge; the only base arrows are its edge and identities, whose degenerate lifts are cocartesian by the mapping criterion.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.4.4, first paragraph: inert lifts and preservation, with cocartesian composition checked by pasting mapping squares.

proof.text: Fix $y=(c,a:p(c)\to o)$ with $s_O(o)=\langle n\rangle$, $s_C(c)=\langle m\rangle$, and active base map $\alpha:\langle m\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$. Choose inert $o\to o_i$ over $\rho_i$. The non-basepoint sets $I_i=\alpha^{-1}(i)$ partition $\langle m\rangle^\circ$. Choose inert block projections $c\to c_i$ onto these sets. Since their images in $\mathcal O^\otimes$ are cocartesian over the block projections, the composite $p(c)\xrightarrow a o\to o_i$ factors through $p(c_i)$, giving an active $a_i:p(c_i)\to o_i$ and a coherent square. These squares give edges $y\to y_i=(c_i,a_i)$ in $H$ which are $r$-cocartesian by step 3 and $(s_Or)$-cocartesian by step 5. A block can be empty, in which case $c_i$ has arity zero and $a_i$ is a nullary operation. If $n=0$, activity forces $m=0$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.4.4, partition of inputs used in the relative-limit verification; Lemma 2.2.4.16, explicit finite-pointed-set blocks.

proof.text:
Verify the entire output mapping-space Segal axiom directly. Write $x=(d,b:p(d)\to t)$ with arities $\ell,k$ and active base $\beta:\langle\ell\rangle\to\langle k\rangle$. For each pointed $u:\langle k\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$, the mapping formula of step 1 expresses $\operatorname{Map}_H^u(x,y)$ as the disjoint union, over pointed maps $v:\langle\ell\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ satisfying $\alpha v=u\beta$, of
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^\otimes}^{v}(d,c)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}^{\alpha v}(p(d),o)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}^{u}(t,o).$$
Here the superscript means the homotopy fiber over that map in the discrete mapping space of $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. The output product axioms in $\mathcal C^\otimes$ and $\mathcal O^\otimes$ decompose each of the three spaces into its block or color factors, and do so compatibly with $p$, since $p$ preserves the chosen inert projections. For the $\mathcal C^\otimes$ factors, group its singleton output factors by $I_i$; this also proves the decomposition for blocks of size zero. The permissible $v$ correspond bijectively to tuples of maps $v_i:\langle\ell\rangle\to(I_i)_+$ with $\alpha_i v_i=\rho_i u\beta$: for an input $j$ with $u\beta(j)=i\ne *$, activity forces exactly its $i$th component to be non-basepoint; if $u\beta(j)=*$ all components must be basepoint. These rules give the unique inverse to block restriction. Products of the path-space pullbacks are the pullback of the products (a tuple of paths is a path in the product), and disjoint unions distribute by this bijection of indices. Thus the actual projection map induces
$$\operatorname{Map}_H^u(x,y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Map}_H^{\rho_i u}(x,y_i).$$
All operations preserve the higher simplices in these path models. For $n=0$, $m=0$, the sole $v$ is the collapse and all displayed mapping spaces to zero-output objects are contractible by the empty-output axiom, so the result is the empty product, a point.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.2.4.4, verification of relative limiting inert cones; explicit mapping-space expansion of the three successive relative-limit checks and Lemma 2.2.4.16.

proof.text: Projection functor and full faithfulness. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to the cocartesian fibration $E_{\rho_i}\to\Delta^1$ of step 5, with $K=H_{\langle n\rangle}$, $A$ its inclusion as the fiber over $0$, $G$ constant at $1$ and $\eta$ the constant transformation along $0\to1$. It gives a coherent functor $\pi_i:H_{\langle n\rangle}\to H_{\langle1\rangle}$ and a coherent transformation $\lambda^i:A\to\pi_i$ with $E_{\rho_i}$-cocartesian components $\lambda^i_x:x\to\pi_ix$. By its case $K=\Delta^0$, precomposition with $\lambda^i_x$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{H_{\langle1\rangle}}(\pi_ix,y')$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{E_{\rho_i}}(x,y')$. That space is $\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i}_H(x,y')$: it is the strict fiber over $\rho_i$ of the map to the discrete $\operatorname{Map}_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}(\langle n\rangle,\langle1\rangle)$, hence the homotopy fiber. The $(s_Or)$-cocartesian edge $y\to y_i$ of step 6 is $E_{\rho_i}$-cocartesian by step 5, so it differs from $\lambda^i_y$ by an equivalence $y_i\simeq\pi_iy$ in $H_{\langle1\rangle}$. Hence step 7 holds with the $\lambda^i_y$ in place of the edges of step 6. The $\pi_i$ form $\pi:H_{\langle n\rangle}\to H_{\langle1\rangle}^n$. Maps in a fiber are the mapping-space fibers over the identity. Naturality of $\lambda^i$ at $w:x\to y$ gives $\pi_i(w)\lambda^i_x\simeq\lambda^i_yw$, so under these identifications the map induced by $\pi$ is postcomposition with the $\lambda^i_y$. This is the equivalence of step 7 with $u=1_{\langle n\rangle}$, so $\pi$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.4.4 (fiber Segal condition of Definition 2.1.1.10(2)): full faithfulness of the colour projection from the output mapping-space condition; transport functors as in HTT Proposition 3.1.2.1 and 2.4.4.2, duals.

proof.text: Essential surjectivity and conclusion. Take any finite family $y_i=(c_i,a_i:p(c_i)\to o_i)$, where $o_i$ has arity one and $c_i$ has arity $m_i$. The fiber product axiom in $\mathcal C^\otimes$ assembles their color lists into $c$ of arity $m=\sum_i m_i$ with inert block maps $c\to c_i$; the analogous axiom in $\mathcal O^\otimes$ assembles the $o_i$ into $o$ of arity $n$. Let $\alpha:\langle m\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$ send the $i$th block to $i$. The output mapping-space axiom in $\mathcal O^\otimes$ supplies an arrow $a:p(c)\to o$ over $\alpha$ with components $a_i p(c\to c_i)$ and the specified homotopies. It is active. The resulting coherent squares give inert-source edges $(c,a)\to y_i$, which are $r$-cocartesian by step 3 and, having inert image $o\to o_i$, $(s_Or)$-cocartesian as in step 5; by step 8 and uniqueness of cocartesian lifts, $\pi_i(c,a)\simeq y_i$. When $n=0$, choose zero-arity objects $c$ and $o$ of the two operads and an equivalence $p(c)\to o$ in the contractible zero fiber of $\mathcal O^\otimes$; this supplies $(c,a)$, while step 7 makes its zero fiber contractible. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to the fully faithful projection functor $\pi$ of step 8: its essential image is the whole target by this construction, so it is an equivalence. With the inner fibration of step 1, inert lifts of step 5 and output mapping-space axiom of step 7, these are exactly the symmetric infinity-operad axioms. Step 5 gives inert preservation by $r$, step 4 its cocartesian fibration and exact edge criterion; all clauses follow.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.4.4, last paragraph: assembling the colorwise objects and operations; the empty family is included explicitly.
